Tourist surges hit small Spanish and European towns, with hotel prices in Spain and Iceland exceeding $1,000/night, though Iceland hotels cut rates closer to the date. Scientists also used the eclipse for solar research. Last comparable eclipse visible from European mainland was 1999. Thursday's UK newspaper front pages were dominated by the eclipse.

clusters.state_of_play: A Fox News poll shows Roy Cooper leading Michael Whatley by 9 points in the North Carolina Senate race, with Democrats holding an enthusiasm edge over Republicans. Democratic Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs has selected former Republican Mayor John Giles, now independent, as her running mate. In Minnesota, progressive Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan won the Democratic Senate primary by 20 points over moderate Rep. Angie Craig, in a race defined by anti-ICE anger following the Trump administration's immigration crackdown. Flanagan, backed by Bernie Sanders and Ilhan Omar, could become the first Native woman in the Senate. Her win is the latest in a series of progressive victories over moderates in the Midwest — including Abdul El-Sayed's Michigan U.S. Senate primary win the prior week — and marks a second straight primary setback for Democratic Senate Leader Chuck Schumer. Flanagan faces baggage from a Minnesota fraud scandal that occurred during her tenure as Lt. Gov. Former TV sports reporter Michele Tafoya won the Republican Senate primary in Minnesota and will face Flanagan in November. Minnesota is the first state to set all-female matchups in both its biggest races: Flanagan vs. Tafoya for Senate, and Klobuchar vs. Demuth for governor. Ilhan Omar has been projected to win the Democratic primary in Minnesota's 5th Congressional District. Sen. Amy Klobuchar has been projected to win the Minnesota DFL gubernatorial primary and will face Minnesota House Speaker Lisa Demuth in November; Demuth defeated Trump-backed MyPillow founder Mike Lindell, who received roughly 31% of the vote. Post-loss, Lindell questioned the vote numbers. In Minnesota's 1st Congressional District, GOP incumbent Brad Finstad survived a primary against challengers Gregory Goetzman and Oliver Morlan. In Connecticut, former Hartford Mayor Luke Bronin has been projected to defeat veteran Democratic incumbent Rep. John Larson in the House primary. Larson's loss makes him the 10th House incumbent to lose a primary this cycle, an unusually high figure driven by Democrats pushing leaders to pass the torch to a younger, more progressive generation and Republicans reckoning with Trump's influence. In Wisconsin, Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley defeated democratic socialist Francesca Hong in a stunningly narrow Democratic gubernatorial primary — winning by less than a percentage point — after re-entering the race and securing an endorsement from outgoing Gov. Tony Evers, who called Crowley 'the future of the party.' Crowley, who could become the state's first Black governor, will face Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany in November. Following her loss, Hong endorsed Crowley. Sabato's Crystal Ball subsequently shifted the Wisconsin governor's race toward Democrats. In South Carolina's special GOP Senate primary, Darline Graham (32.6%) and Rep. Ralph Norman (24%) have advanced to an Aug. 25 runoff, with Rep. Russell Fry finishing third at 20.3%. Trump-backed Graham denied being a 'nepo senator.' Trump's endorsements have broadly flopped in major statewide governor races: in addition to Lindell, Trump-backed Andy Ogles (TN) and Amir Hassan (MI) also lost their primaries; Hassan lost to Thomas Smith. An analysis by G. Elliott Morris found that primary election polls miss by an average of 13 points, and prediction markets were also shown to have failed on the Hong result in Wisconsin.

items.title: Recapping Europe's first total solar eclipse in 27 years

clusters.state_of_play: A total solar eclipse — the only one of 2026 and Spain's first in over a century — occurred on Aug. 12, 2026, with a path of totality crossing Greenland, Iceland, and northern Spain (approx. 2 min totality). Tens of millions across western Europe, including the UK and Iceland, witnessed the event, with more than 90% of the Sun covered in the UK and more than 95% in Cornwall. Thousands flocked to viewing spots including Sasamón, Spain; trains were packed and carpools booked. Tourist surges hit small Spanish and European towns, with hotel prices in Spain and Iceland exceeding $1,000/night, though Iceland hotels cut rates closer to the date. On-the-ground reporters included CBS News meteorologist Rob Marciano in Mallorca, France 24's Sarah Morris in Segovia, NBC News's Gadi Schwartz, and eclipse chaser Chris Orion in Sasamón. Scientists also used the eclipse for solar research. Last comparable eclipse visible from European mainland was 1999. Thursday's UK newspaper front pages were dominated by the eclipse.

clusters.title: US inflation falls to 3.4% in July

items.title: US inflation falls to 3.4% in July

ledger.unique: Iran war fallout framed as continuing to reverberate across economy.

clusters.state_of_play: The BLS released the July CPI on Wednesday showing prices rose 3.4% year-over-year and 0.1% month-over-month, in line with expectations. Energy prices fell 1.5% in July but remain 14.7% above a year ago, with the Iran war cited as an ongoing drag. Gasoline and grocery prices also fell. The data reinforces the Fed's patient approach to rate hikes but has not resolved the internal debate; a September hike is now seen as less likely. Markets were steady on the news. Separately, South Africa's unemployment hit a four-year high with 8.5 million jobless.
